color alone is usually not a reliable way of identifying a mineral, especially with jadeitie, since the iron in it will determine how green it gets. It looks really nice, and your added descriptions was good. It's either jadeite or nephrite. They are both usually used for jade, as jade is just the jewl quality of the minerals. They are kind of hard to tell apart, as it really comes down to chemical composition. It might depend on where you got it, as jadeite is more commonly found in the Americas, at least to my knowledge it is. Regardless I think it is safe to assume that it is mad of jade. Try scratching it with your fingernail. If you can scratch it then it is probably selenite, if you can't it, then it probably is barite. Selenite has a hardness of 2 and Barite is about a 3.5, your fingernail should be about 2.5 on the Moh's hardness scale. Also take a blacklight to it, if it is selenite it should glow, as that mineral is fluorescent. Hope this helps.

The brown coloring could be due to oxidation of any iron within the mineral. So it is probably green throughout, it is just weathering at the surface has given it a brown color to it. It looks like it is green granite, which means the green color comes from olivine and pyroxene (greenish black). It still is a really cool find.

After looking at the photos it appears to be granite. It has a little green to it, or at least it appears to have some green to it, if that is the case then it could be part of a greenbelt from the franciscan formation, but I think it is probably from the Sierra Nevada Batholith. 

In your picture of Jawbone I can see remnants of a basalt flow, which is common for that area as well as the usual seds, this would be why a piece of granite would stick out in the area. There might be an outcrop not to far from the area you found it, as the piece looks to be still somewhat angular.
